userStories.title: Apply exact description and acceptance-criterion edits independently
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend flow-prd-edits.ts with ordered exact-text description and criterion edits and per-edit refusals.

**Motivation** — Phase 9 runs once with permission to edit `prd.json`; it patches the PRD surgically against a pre-edit snapshot and ends READY-WITH-EDITS, and the run starts.

**Approach** — **Edits are exact-text, applied in order, each on its own.** An edit names the text it replaces (the snapshot check). One whose text is not found, or not unique, is refused and reported; the others still apply. A refused edit never stops the flow.

**`applyPrdEditsToText`:** `JSON.parse(prdText)`; not an object with a `userStories` array -> `unreadable`. Edits
apply in input order to the evolving document.
A story is found by `id === edit.story` (none -> `unknown story`). Per op:
- `replace_description`: a story whose `description` is not a string is refused `story malformed`; `old` must occur
  exactly once in it (0 -> `text not found`, 2+ -> `text not unique`); `new === old` -> `no change`; that
  occurrence is replaced by `new`.
- `replace_ac` / `remove_ac`: a story whose `acceptanceCriteria` is not an array is refused `story malformed`; `old`
  must equal exactly one entry (0 -> `text not found`, 2+ -> `text not unique`); `replace_ac` with `new === old` ->
  `no change`; `replace_ac` whose `new` equals another entry -> `duplicate criterion`; the entry is replaced, or
  removed. Removing the last entry is refused `last criterion` (nax rejects a
  story with no acceptance criteria).
- `add_ac`: a non-array `acceptanceCriteria` -> `story malformed`; an entry equal to `new` already present ->
  `duplicate criterion`; else `new` is appended.
- `applied` counts the edits that changed the document. The result text is `JSON.stringify(document, null, 2) +
  '\n'`; every key the edits do not touch is kept.

**Scope** — In: JSON document read, story lookup, replace_description/replace_ac/remove_ac/add_ac, ordered mutation and refusal bookkeeping, and flow-prd-edits-apply.spec.ts. Out: context-file operations, limit handling and final serialization edge-case coverage (US-003); forge writes (US-007/008). Editing PRD fields other than a story's `description`, `acceptanceCriteria` and `contextFiles` (ids, order, `dependencies`, `outOfScope`, `analysis`, routing).

**Interface** — Verbatim shared result and function contract:
```ts
export type PrdEditsResult =
  | { kind: 'ok'; text: string; applied: number; refused: FlowPrdEditRefusal[] }
  | { kind: 'unreadable' };
/** Apply the edits, in order, to the text of a prd.json. */
export function applyPrdEditsToText(prdText: string, edits: FlowPrdEdit[]): PrdEditsResult;
```
Use US-001's types and report original zero-based input indexes even when earlier edits were refused.

userStories.title: Complete context-file edits, bounded application and stable PRD output
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete applyPrdEditsToText with context-file mutations, edit/text limits, unreadable results and deterministic output.

**Motivation** — A re-plan happens only when the spec needs new content: a re-plan drops qualifiers added to existing text, so it can undo fixes.

**Approach** — **`applyPrdEditsToText`:** `JSON.parse(prdText)`; not an object with a `userStories` array -> `unreadable`. Edits
apply in input order to the evolving document. The edit at 0-based `index >= FLOW_PRD_EDITS_MAX` is refused
`over limit`. A `replace_description`, `replace_ac` or `add_ac` whose `new` is longer than `FLOW_PRD_EDIT_TEXT_MAX`
code units is refused `text too long`. A story is found by `id === edit.story` (none -> `unknown story`).
- `add_context_file`: `path` must be relative, without a `..` segment, a leading `/` or a backslash (else
  `invalid path`); a `contextFiles` that is present and not an array -> `story malformed`; a path already listed ->
  `duplicate path`; else it is appended (a missing `contextFiles` array is created).
- `remove_context_file`: `path` must be in `contextFiles` (else `path not listed`); it is removed.
- `applied` counts the edits that changed the document. The result text is `JSON.stringify(document, null, 2) +
  '\n'`; every key the edits do not touch is kept.

**The verdict has an 8 KB budget.** The runner keeps the last `AGENT_RESULT_LIMITS.maxOutputBytes` (8,192) bytes of an agent's output (`packages/fleet-protocol/src/agent-jobs.ts`), and `parseFlowVerdict` finds the verdict by its `{"findings"` prefix. So the edits instruction asks for `findings` as the first key and the whole JSON line under 6,000 bytes of UTF-8, and the caps are `FLOW_PRD_EDITS_MAX` = 12 edits of at most `FLOW_PRD_EDIT_TEXT_MAX` = 400 code units of new text (a longer `new` is refused `text too long`, never cut). A verdict that still overflows is `verdict_unreadable` (accepted; the instruction tells the reviewer to keep the most important edits and report the rest as one minor finding).

**Scope** — In: completion of the upstream pure module and flow-prd-edits-files.spec.ts covering path operations, caps, unreadable documents and exact output. Out: description/criterion base algorithms (US-002), prompt and verdict transport (US-004), forge writes (US-007/008). Editing PRD fields other than a story's `description`, `acceptanceCriteria` and `contextFiles` (ids, order, `dependencies`, `outOfScope`, `analysis`, routing).

**Interface** — `export function applyPrdEditsToText(prdText: string, edits: FlowPrdEdit[]): PrdEditsResult;` Keep the existing result union, 12-edit cap and 400-code-unit text cap from US-001. Do not truncate overlong replacements or change keys outside the editable fields.

userStories.title: Carry PRD edits through verdict parsing and opt-in phase-9 tasks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend review verdicts and opt-in PRD_REVIEW tasks to transport typed edits while preserving legacy tasks.

**Motivation** — Phase 9 runs once with permission to edit `prd.json`; it patches the PRD surgically against a pre-edit snapshot and ends READY-WITH-EDITS, and the run starts.

**Approach** — `parseFlowVerdict` reads an optional `prdEdits` key of the same JSON object through `parsePrdEdits`; absent ->
`[]`; present and `parsePrdEdits` returns `null` -> `{ ok: false }`.
**`parseFlowVerdict` is step-agnostic.** A malformed `prdEdits` key makes any verdict unreadable, including a `SPEC_REVIEW` one; only the `PRD_REVIEW` task asks for edits, so the case is not expected.

With `step === 'PRD_REVIEW'` and `options.prdEdits === true`, the suffix is
`\n\n${FLOW_CALLS_PRECEDENCE}\n\n${FLOW_VERDICT_INSTRUCTION}\n\n${FLOW_PRD_EDITS_INSTRUCTION}`; otherwise unchanged.
`BuildStepDispatchInput` gains `prdEdits?: boolean`; the review case calls
`buildReviewTask(step, feature.specPath, feature.feature, { prdEdits: input.prdEdits === true })`.

`FLOW_PRD_EDITS_INSTRUCTION` (in `flow-steps.ts`, exact text):
```text
Fix every PRD defect you can yourself, as edits, instead of reporting it. Add a "prdEdits" array to the same JSON object, after "findings": the object must still start with {"findings".
Each edit is one of: {"story":"<id>","op":"replace_description","old":"<exact text in the description>","new":"<text>"}, {"story":"<id>","op":"replace_ac","old":"<exact criterion>","new":"<criterion>"}, {"story":"<id>","op":"remove_ac","old":"<exact criterion>"}, {"story":"<id>","op":"add_ac","new":"<criterion>"}, {"story":"<id>","op":"add_context_file","path":"<repo path>"}, {"story":"<id>","op":"remove_context_file","path":"<repo path>"}.
Edit only a story's description, acceptance criteria and context files. Never remove a criterion that carries a spec acceptance criterion. Do not report or edit "analysis": it reaches no prompt.
Keep the whole JSON line under 6000 bytes of UTF-8 and at most 12 edits; when more are needed, keep the most important edits and report the rest as one minor finding.
Report a finding only when the spec itself must change or only the user can decide. Do not edit any file: the flow commits your edits.
```

**Scope** — In: flow-verdict.ts, flow-steps.ts, flow-step-dispatch.ts and their existing unit specs; successful-parse whole-object assertions gain prdEdits: [], the findings themselves and every failure case are unchanged. Existing three-argument buildReviewTask expectations and dispatch bodies without the flag remain unchanged. Out: pure edit parsing implementation (US-001), setting the flag in advance (US-009), decision actions (US-006/010), forge commits (US-007/008). Thread-entry flows: their review task, findings stop and PRD are unchanged. Raising the agent output limit (`AGENT_RESULT_LIMITS.maxOutputBytes`); a verdict over it stays `verdict_unreadable`.

**Interface** — Verbatim target declarations:
```ts
export type FlowVerdict = { ok: true; findings: FlowFinding[]; prdEdits: FlowPrdEdit[] } | { ok: false };
buildReviewTask(step: ReviewStep, specPath: string, feature: string, options?: { prdEdits?: boolean }): string
```
A verdict longer than the 8 KB output tail has its `{"findings"` prefix cut -> `verdict_unreadable` (accepted). Seam tests must show parseFlowVerdict uses parsePrdEdits, and buildStepDispatch forwards the opt-in to buildReviewTask.

userStories.title: Decide two spec passes and no-findings PRD edit application
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the PRD-edit action contract and the two-pass SPEC_REVIEW and empty-findings PRD_REVIEW decision rules.

**Motivation** — Spec review runs pass 1, the findings are verified and folded, pass 2 runs, and its findings are folded without a third review.

**Approach** — Decision rules (`decideFlowStep`, `SPEC_REVIEW` and `PRD_REVIEW` COMPLETED with a readable verdict; every rule not listed is unchanged, in its current order, including the ambiguity, findings-cap and `canApplyCalls` rules):
1. `SPEC_REVIEW`, no findings -> `dispatch PLAN` (unchanged).
2. `SPEC_REVIEW`, `callsJobId === job.id` -> `dispatch SPEC_REVIEW` when `specReviewCount !== undefined &&
   specReviewCount < 2`, else `dispatch PLAN`. (Before: always `PLAN`.) An absent count keeps today's behaviour, so
   the rule changes nothing until the advance service supplies the count (US-009).
3. `PRD_REVIEW`, no findings: `canApplyCalls` true, `verdict.prdEdits.length > 0` and `prdEditsJobId !== job.id` ->
   `apply_prd_edits` with `accepted: []`; otherwise `dispatch RUN`. (Before: always `RUN`.)

`FlowStepInput` gains `specReviewCount?: number` and `prdEditsJobId?: string | null`; `FlowStepAction`
gains `{ kind: 'apply_prd_edits'; jobId: string; edits: FlowPrdEdit[]; accepted: FlowFinding[] }`, and
`export type ApplyPrdEditsAction = Extract<FlowStepAction, { kind: 'apply_prd_edits' }>` .

**The findings cap still stops.** More than `FLOW_CALLS_MAX_FINDINGS` (20) findings in one verdict stops `review_findings` in every round, as today.

**Scope** — In: new decision input/action types, rules 1–3 and their unit cases in flow-step-decision.spec.ts. Existing cases are unchanged (they pass no specReviewCount, which keeps dispatch PLAN, and no PRD_REVIEW verdict in them carries edits). Preserve first-round PRD findings on the calls/re-plan path and ignore edits there. Out: rule 4's second-round finding acceptance (US-010), reading counts/marker in advance (US-009), handling the new action in advance (US-010), edit commits (US-007/008). A third `SPEC_REVIEW` pass, or a configurable number of passes. Thread-entry flows: their review task, findings stop and PRD are unchanged.

**Interface** — Verbatim target additions:
```ts
specReviewCount?: number
prdEditsJobId?: string | null
{ kind: 'apply_prd_edits'; jobId: string; edits: FlowPrdEdit[]; accepted: FlowFinding[] }
export type ApplyPrdEditsAction = Extract<FlowStepAction, { kind: 'apply_prd_edits' }>;
```
The optional count preserves old callers. When canApplyCalls is false, PRD edits are ignored and existing thread review behavior remains unchanged.

userStories.title: Commit applicable PRD edits on the expected flow branch head
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add FleetFlowCallsService.applyPrdEdits for expected-head PRD contents commits and unchanged/guard outcomes.

**Motivation** — Phase 9 runs once with permission to edit `prd.json`; it patches the PRD surgically against a pre-edit snapshot and ends READY-WITH-EDITS, and the run starts.

**Approach** — **The API commits the edits, not the agent.** An `AGENT` job's checkout is detached and nothing it writes is pushed
(`apps/runner/src/executor/checkout.ts`, the `AGENT` branch of `prepareCheckout`). The reviewer returns the edits in
its verdict and koda applies them through the contents API, as it commits Flow's calls. No runner change: a `RUN`
whose runner-local branch is behind origin checks out origin (`planBranch` -> `from-origin`), so the edit commit is
what `RUN` builds on.
**The commit lives on `FleetFlowCallsService`** (`applyPrdEdits`), next to `apply`: it is the flow's forge-write owner, and a new injected service would change the positional constructor of `FleetFlowAdvanceService` in five specs.

`applyPrdEdits` (on `FleetFlowCallsService`): `action.edits` empty -> `{ kind: 'unchanged', refused: [] }` with no
forge call. Otherwise, mirroring `apply`: no feature -> `failed` `feature missing`; repo missing or not installed ->
`failed` `repo not connected`. The path is `.nax/features/<feature>/prd.json` of the flow's single feature; mint an
installation token; read the branch head; read the file at that head (missing -> `failed`,
`prd.json missing on <branch>`). When the head equals `expectedHead`: `applyPrdEditsToText` on the file
(`unreadable` -> `failed`, `prd.json unreadable`); `applied === 0` -> `unchanged`; else `putFile` with message
`chore(<feature>): flow PRD edits from PRD_REVIEW job <jobId>` -> `committed` with the commit sha;

**Scope** — In: method and exported outcome union, feature/repo guards, empty/all-refused unchanged results, pinned-head file read, pure helper seam and single contents write; add cases to fleet-flow-calls.service.spec.ts while existing apply cases remain unchanged. Out: moved-head recovery and write/error classifications (US-008), decision handling/marker/activity (US-010). Runner changes: the `RUN` checkout already prefers origin when the runner-local branch is behind. No forge HTTP within a transaction, and no token in flow state, logs or activity.

**Interface** — Verbatim target:

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete applyPrdEdits with strict own-commit recovery, stale-head results and permanent/transient write classification.

**Motivation** — A re-plan happens only when the spec needs new content: a re-plan drops qualifiers added to existing text, so it can undo fixes.

**Approach** — `refused` ->
`failed` `prd.json write refused`; `conflict` -> re-read: same blob sha -> `failed` `prd.json write refused`, else

true and the file at the head equals `applyPrdEditsToText(<file at expectedHead as UTF-8 text>, action.edits).text` -> `committed` with
`sha: head`; otherwise `stale`. A `RepoCheckException` maps through `callsOutcomeForForgeError` (`failed` with its
reason, else `retry`).

Branch head moved since the PLAN -> `stale` -> re-ask (as for calls), unless the move is our own edit commit (recovered as `committed`).
Write refused (`refused`, or `conflict` with the same blob) -> `failed` -> stop `calls_failed` `PRD_REVIEW edits: prd.json write refused`.
Forge transient error / `conflict` with a moved blob -> `retry`: the next tick decides again.

Out: applying the outcome to the live flow, stopping or re-asking (US-010), document mutation (US-002/003). ```ts

userStories.title: Apply PRD edits in advance and accept remaining post-replan findings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Execute apply_prd_edits passes with guarded forge writes and durable activity, accepting second-round findings and then dispatching RUN.

**Motivation** — The rule "any finding in the second PRD round stops the flow" has no counterpart in the manual process the flow automates.

**Approach** — Decision rule 4 (`decideFlowStep`, `PRD_REVIEW` COMPLETED with a readable verdict):
`PRD_REVIEW` with findings, after the unchanged ambiguity, cap and `canApplyCalls` rules: let
`replan = planCount < 2 || hasCurrentAnswers`. `replan` true -> the current calls path (`callsJobId === job.id` ->
`dispatch PLAN`, else `apply_calls`), the edits are ignored. `replan` false -> `prdEditsJobId === job.id` ->
`dispatch RUN`; otherwise `apply_prd_edits` with the verdict's `prdEdits` and `accepted` = the findings. (Before:
`replan` false stopped `review_findings`.) Rule 4's `apply_prd_edits` outcome ships with the advance pass that
handles it (US-010); until then `decide` would hand the action to `writeDecision`, which has no handler for it.
Here `hasCurrentAnswers` is `input.questionsJobId === latestJob.id && input.answers !== null`; keep the existing ambiguity wait and answer-attachment behavior before selecting the calls/re-plan or PRD-edit path.

**Second-round findings are accepted, not committed as calls.** After the re-plan the spec no longer changes what is built (`RUN` reads `prd.json`); the accepted findings' summaries are kept in the `flow.prd_edits` activity record.
**The findings cap still stops.** More than `FLOW_CALLS_MAX_FINDINGS` (20) findings in one verdict stops `review_findings` in every round, as today.
**A failed edit commit reuses the `calls_failed` stop reason** with the detail `PRD_REVIEW edits: <detail>`, so the stop-reason union, the web labels and the stop ticket stay as they are.

Advance (`FleetFlowAdvanceService`):
- `DispatchPass` also admits `ApplyPrdEditsAction`, and the kind check lets `apply_prd_edits` through to a pass (otherwise it would reach `writeDecision` and the flow would never move); `advance` calls a new `advancePrdEdits`.
- `decide`: `apply_prd_edits` takes the `apply_calls` `PRD_REVIEW` branch (the condition becomes
  `action.kind === 'apply_prd_edits' || (action.kind === 'apply_calls' && action.step === 'PRD_REVIEW')`, since the
  new action has no `step`): it is not billed (`remaining '0.0000'`),
  the creator-access check applies, it needs the latest `PLAN` with `resultBranch` and `resultSha`, and it persists a
  different PLAN output branch with `setBranch` and the `flow.branch` record exactly as `apply_calls` does.
- `advancePrdEdits(flow, action, plan, now)`: `calls.applyPrdEdits(flow, action, plan.resultSha)`, outside any
  transaction. `retry` -> nothing; `failed` -> `writeStop(flow, 'calls_failed', 'PRD_REVIEW edits: <detail>', now)`;
  otherwise under `lockLive` (nothing when the flow is no longer live): `stale` -> `flowService.reaskLocked(current,
  head, now)`; `committed` / `unchanged` -> `steps.recordPrdEdits(current.id, featureId, action.jobId)` and one
  `record(current, 'flow PRD edits', 'flow.prd_edits', { jobId, sha, applied, refused, accepted })` where `sha` is
  the commit sha or `null`, `applied` is the count (0 for `unchanged`), `refused` is the refusal list, and `accepted`
  is the array of `truncateFlowText(summary, FLOW_CALL_TEXT_MAX)` of the accepted findings (an unsanitised lone
  surrogate would fail the JSON write after the forge commit, on every tick).

Flow stopped or re-asked between the commit and the record -> `lockLive` finds it no longer live: nothing is recorded (as for calls).
No edits, or every edit refused -> `unchanged`: no commit, `prdEditsJobId` recorded, then `RUN`.
Thread-entry flow -> No edits instruction in the task; `prdEdits` ignored; findings stop as today.

**Scope** — In: rule 4 and action pass routing, advancePrdEdits, creator/PLAN/branch guards, outcome handling, atomic marker/activity recording and next-tick RUN. Extend the upstream-created fleet-flow-advance-prd-edits.spec.ts. Out: pure edit algorithms (US-001–003), forge service implementation (US-007/008), schema/repository implementation (US-005), full database loop (US-011). Committing the accepted second-round PRD findings to the spec as Flow's calls. A new stop reason for a failed PRD edit commit; it uses `calls_failed`. Lifting the 20-findings cap for second-round PRD findings. Thread-entry flows: their review task, findings stop and PRD are unchanged. Web and CLI display of `prdEditsJobId` or the `flow.prd_edits` record. Changing the RULE, REVIEW or FIX steps.

**Interface** — Reuse the verbatim contract and action:
```ts
{ kind: 'apply_prd_edits'; jobId: string; edits: FlowPrdEdit[]; accepted: FlowFinding[] }
export type ApplyPrdEditsAction = Extract<FlowStepAction, { kind: 'apply_prd_edits' }>;
applyPrdEdits(flow: FleetFlowRecord, action: ApplyPrdEditsAction, expectedHead: string): Promise<PrdEditsOutcome>
recordPrdEdits(flowId: string, featureId: string, jobId: string): Promise<void>
```

Keep creator checks before forge writes, do not bill edits, and retain approval-generation fencing in lockLive.
